page.name: Logistics & delivery
page.metaDescription: Dispatch notices, arrival windows, failed-delivery rescheduling and proof-of-delivery over the provider accounts you already own.
page.lede: A delivery operation lives on contact attempts: the customer who is not home, the gate code nobody has, the parcel heading back to the depot. Each of those is a message that either saves a second trip or causes one.

sections.h: The messages that save a second attempt
bullets: Dispatch confirmation with a tracking reference
Day-of delivery window, updated when the route changes
Driver-arriving notice ahead of the stop
Failed-delivery notice with a one-tap reschedule link
Depot-collection reminder before a parcel is returned

sections.h: Batches that drain, and receipts you can read
p: Delivery messaging is bursty: a route is planned, a batch goes out, then nothing. On the SMS channel the platform spreads the batch to the pacing your provider allows per number, routes around an account that stops accepting traffic, so a batch does not stall partway through. Receipts come back normalized, which is what tells a failed delivery apart from a message that never arrived.
bullets: Batches spread across connected accounts instead of hammering one
Automatic failover between connected SMS accounts
Receipt status normalized across providers into one webhook payload

sections.h: It fits next to the systems you already run
p: Routing, parcel data and your transport management system stay where they are. The platform sends the message you ask it to send, on the account you connected, and reports what happened to it — which makes it a clean fit next to the systems that already know the route.

faq.q: Can I send a batch of delivery notices without hitting a rate limit?
faq.a: The platform paces SMS to the limit your provider applies per sender number, and you can add further numbers or accounts to raise the ceiling. It does not override your provider’s limit for you.

faq.q: How do I know a notice was actually delivered?
faq.a: Providers return delivery receipts, and the platform normalizes them into a single status. Note that a receipt reflects acceptance by the destination network, not that a human read the message.

faq.q: Can the same notice go out on WhatsApp as well?
faq.a: You can connect the accounts you already hold on each channel and send on whichever you choose. Routing and automatic failover between accounts are implemented on the SMS channel today.
